question: Employment generation became a focus in later Five-Year Plans. Which Five-Year Plan introduced the Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Seventh Plan
Fourth Plan
Fifth Plan
Sixth Plan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sixth Plan

Explanation:
The Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) was launched during India's Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985). Its primary objectives were poverty alleviation and employment generation in rural areas. Under IRDP, rural families were provided assistance through income-generating assets, training, and credit. This programme reflected the growing focus on employment creation in later Five-Year Plans. The Sixth Plan prioritized rural development and employment, laying the foundation for initiatives like IRDP. The programme aimed to uplift below-poverty-line families by providing sustainable livelihood opportunities.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which plan introduced IRDP? → Sixth Five-Year Plan
☛ What was the main objective of IRDP? → Rural poverty alleviation and employment generation
☛ What assistance did IRDP provide? → Income-generating assets, training, and credit
☛ Which plan emphasized employment generation? → Sixth Plan and subsequent plans
☛ What sector did IRDP focus on? → Rural development
question_hi: रोजगार सृजन बाद की पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं में एक फोकस बन गया। किस पंचवर्षीय योजना में एकीकृत ग्रामीण विकास कार्यक्रम (आईआरडीपी) शुरू किया गया था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)

question: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme is aimed at boosting manufacturing. Which of the following sectors is NOT covered under the PLI scheme? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 3)

question: In which year was the PM JI-VAN (Biofuel-Vatra Sukla Crop Residue Removal) scheme launched? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: 2018
2019
2020
2017
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2019

Explanation:
The PM JI-VAN (Biofuel-Vatra Sukla Crop Residue Removal) scheme was launched in the year 2019. The scheme aims to promote the production of biofuels in India and reduce environmental pollution caused by crop residue burning. It provides financial support for second-generation (2G) ethanol projects. Under this scheme, the central government has approved 12 commercial projects and 10 demonstration projects. This helps farmers avoid burning crop residues and contributes to environmental protection.

question: The Planning Commission was the apex body responsible for formulating Five-Year Plans. In which year was the Planning Commission of India established? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (09/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1948
1950
1952
1951
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1950

Explanation:
The Planning Commission of India was established on 15 March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India. It was a non-constitutional body, primarily responsible for formulating and implementing Five-Year Plans for the country's economic development. The first Chairman of the Planning Commission was Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The Commission played a pivotal role in shaping India's development strategy until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015. The correct answer is 1950.

☛ Nature of Planning Commission? → Non-constitutional body
☛ First Chairman of Planning Commission? → Jawaharlal Nehru

☛ Which body replaced Planning Commission? → NITI Aayog

question: Which of the following does not represent the things that make a ‘Smart City’, under the smart city campaign? (RRB NTPC Tier I (27/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Affordable housing, especially for the poor.
Adequate water supply.
Free health and education.
Sustainable environment.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Free health and education.

Explanation:
The Smart City Mission aims to equip cities with infrastructure, technology, and services to improve the quality of life for citizens. Key elements of a smart city include affordable housing, adequate water supply, and a sustainable environment. However, free health and education are not core components of the smart city framework; they are part of welfare schemes. The focus of a smart city is on smart governance, smart mobility, and smart infrastructure. Therefore, providing free health and education does not represent the things that make a smart city under this campaign.

question: Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) operates under the aegis of: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (28/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: Ministry of Human Resource Development
Ministry of Defence
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Home Affairs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

Explanation:
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) was originally under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, but was transferred to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in 2018. It aims to provide vocational training to non-literate and neo-literate persons aged 15 years and above, especially rural and urban poor. JSS operates through voluntary organizations and runs courses aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF). As of 2023-24, there are about 300 JSSs functioning across India.

☛ Which ministry earlier governed JSS? → Ministry of Labour and Employment.
☛ Which framework does JSS follow? → National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).
☛ When was JSS established? → In 1967.

question: When was Project Tiger launched in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1970
1973
1975
1980
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1973

Explanation:
Project Tiger was launched in India on April 1, 1973. Its objective was to conserve the declining population of tigers and protect their natural habitats. question: Which of the following rural housing schemes by the Government of India is re-structured into Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/01/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following schemes of the Govt. of India aims at enhancing the livelihood security of people in rural areas by guaranteeing hundred days of wage-employment? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:

Its primary objective is to enhance the livelihood security of people in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. This act aims to create durable assets and reduce poverty in rural India. PMJDY focuses on financial inclusion, PMGSY on rural road development, and Skilled India Yojana on skill development. question: Which scheme of the Government of India facilitates bank loans between Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore to at least one scheduled caste/ scheduled tribe borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up greenfield enterprises? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following is a government initiated insurance scheme, administered by LIC, for rural landless households? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 2)

solution:

question: When was 'Antyodaya Anna Yojana' launched? (RRB JE ME (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: October 2000
December 2000
August 2001
October 2002
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is December 2000

Explanation:
The Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) was launched by the Government of India in December 2000 as a food security scheme. Its objective is to provide highly subsidized food grains to the poorest families below the poverty line (BPL). Under the scheme, each eligible family receives 35 kg of rice or wheat per month through the Public Distribution System (PDS). Initially covering 1 crore families, the scheme was later expanded and now reaches approximately 2.5 crore families. AAY is now subsumed under the National Food Security Act, 2013, ensuring legal entitlement to food grains. This scheme plays a crucial role in reducing hunger and malnutrition among the most vulnerable sections of society.

question: Which mission was launched by the Govt. of India in December 2014 to achieve full immunisation coverage for all children and pregnant women at a rapid pace? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Mission Indradhanush
Sukanya yojana

solution:

Explanation:
In December 2014, the Government of India launched Mission Indradhanush to rapidly achieve full immunisation coverage for all children and pregnant women. The mission targeted children who were left out or dropped out from routine vaccination. It provided vaccination against 7 diseases: diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, polio, tuberculosis, measles, and hepatitis B. Later, it was upgraded to the Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI). This mission significantly increased full immunisation coverage to over 90% in many areas.

question: Which of the following options is NOT correct regarding Swachh Bharat Abhiyan? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (10/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: The main goal of the campaign was to eradicate the practice of open defecation.

It is the restructuring of Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan
It's main focus is achieving cleanliness only in urban areas of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It's main focus is achieving cleanliness only in urban areas of India.

Explanation:
Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on October 2, 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Its primary goals were to eradicate open defecation and improve solid waste management. The campaign is focused on both rural and urban areas, not just urban areas. The rural component is called Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) and the urban component is called Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban). It is a restructuring of the earlier Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, which was launched in 2012. Therefore, option 4 is incorrect to state it only focuses on urban areas.

Explanation:

question: Which of the following scheme was launched in April 2020 to enable an integrated property validation solution for rural India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: SVAMITVA
SAMARTH
UMANG
KUSUM
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is SVAMITVA

Explanation:
SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) scheme was launched in April 2020 to enable an integrated property validation solution for rural India. The scheme aims to update land records and provide property cards to rural residents. This gives them legal proof of property ownership, enabling access to financial services like bank loans. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and state governments through drone surveys. SVAMITVA helps strengthen the rural economy and reduce land disputes.
